predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Rome, a Byzantine administrative division, the older papal holdings

predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Lombards
predecessors.text: the exarchate of Ravenna and the Pentapolis, conquered by Aistulf in 751 and given to the pope by Pepin in 756

predecessors.name: Exarchate of Ravenna
predecessors.text: the former Byzantine exarchate, 'finally fell to the Lombards in 751'

successors.name: Kingdom of Italy
successors.text: Rome and Lazio, annexed by the royal decree of 9 October 1870

successors.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
successors.text: the Legations (1859-60 through the United Provinces of Central Italy), and the Marche and Umbria (November 1860)

ledger.x: 756: Pepin's gift makes the pope a temporal sovereign.
756: the exarchate of Ravenna and the Pentapolis pass to the pope.
757: the Lombard duchy of Ferrara pledged to the pope.
763: Emilia (Bologna, Imola, Ferrara) joins the shape.
775: the shape withdraws to the Duchy of Rome after Charlemagne is king of the Lombards.
781: Charlemagne's reputed extension of papal lands.
793: the shape shrinks by about 5,000 km2.
1198: Innocent III's papacy acquires the March of Ancona.
1208: the Este become lords of Ferrara under the pope.
1272: Umbria joins the shape.
1274: the Comtat Venaissin becomes papal territory, a detached dependency in Provence.
1278: Rudolf I cedes Romagna.
1309: the court moves to Avignon.
1348: the popes buy Avignon.
1376: the papacy returns to Rome; the page's text dates the end of the Avignon papacy to 1378 and Albornoz's restoration of papal control to the Constitutiones Aegidianae of 29 April 1357.
1500: Cesare Borgia carves out the Duchy of Romagna.
1503: the Duchy of Romagna falls with the Borgia.
1506: Julius II marches on Bologna and Perugia.
ledger.cp: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia

ledger.x: 1507: the despots are gone.
ledger.cp: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia

ledger.x: 1507: Cliopatria's shape widens by about 1,050 km2 on its western edge (to 10.86 E, towards Modena and the Bologna hills), the year the Bologna campaign ended (23 March 1507).
ledger.cp: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia

ledger.x: 1509: the pope and the League of Cambrai against Venice in Romagna.
1509: Agnadello leads to the recovery of Romagna.
1512: Parma and Piacenza fall to the pope.
1545: Parma and Piacenza become a duchy for Paul III's son.
1597: the main Este line dies out.
1597: the pope takes Ferrara and Comacchio. the page states the Papal States took Ferrara in 1597; Comacchio was claimed the same way; the Este kept Modena and Reggio.
1631: the Duchy of Urbino is reclaimed.
1649: the Duchy of Castro is annexed.
1768: French troops occupy the Comtat Venaissin and Avignon.
1774: the French occupation of the Comtat and Avignon ends.
14 September 1791: the Comtat votes to join France.
14 September 1791: Avignon goes with the Comtat to revolutionary France.
1796: the French seize the Legations.
February 1797: the occupation of the Legations becomes a cession.
19 February 1797: Tolentino strips the Legations.
15 February 1798: Rome becomes a republic.
June 1800: the Papal States are restored.
2 April 1808: the Marche go to Napoleon's Kingdom of Italy.
17 May 1809: Rome is annexed to the French Empire.
1814: the Papal States are restored.
9 February 1849: the Roman Republic is proclaimed.

3 July 1849: French troops end the Roman Republic. the French Army entered Rome on 3 July 1849 and re-established the Holy See's temporal power; Pius IX returned in April 1850 (a 'Red Triumvirate' of cardinals governed until then); French soldiers who had propped up the papal administration stayed…

1859: the Legations break away. the Kingdom of Sardinia invaded the Papal State and set up a military government, the United Provinces of Central Italy, which included the Romagne; in December 1859 Tuscany formed a union with Modena, Parma and the Papal Legations (United Provinces…
11 September 1860: Sardinia invades the Marche and Umbria.
29 September 1860: Ancona surrenders to Sardinia after the siege that followed Castelfidardo.
November 1860: the Marche and Umbria vote to join Sardinia.
November 1860: the fighting over the Marche and Umbria ends in annexation.
11 September 1870: the Italian army enters the Papal States.
20 September 1870: Porta Pia.
20 September 1870: Rome falls and the Papal States end.

wars.name: Frankish campaigns against the Lombards (Pepin and Aistulf)
wars.outcome: Pepin crossed Mont Cenis in spring 755 and beat the Lombards near Susa (First Peace of Pavia); Aistulf besieged Rome from 1 January 756; a second Frankish army in April 756 forced the Second Peace of Pavia, with hostages, tribute and a written promise to…

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom
wars.outcome: Hadrian I asked for help against the Lombards; Charlemagne besieged Pavia in 774 and took the title King of the Lombards after Desiderius surrendered.

wars.name: Cesare Borgia's conquest of Romagna
wars.outcome: Cesare Borgia carved out an ephemeral Duchy of Romagna in 1500; after Alexander VI died his lands were taken by Julius II.

wars.name: Julius II's campaign against Bologna and Perugia
wars.outcome: The pope personally led the campaign (Bologna, 17 August 1506 to 23 March 1507) that freed Perugia and Bologna from their despots; Perugia 'voluntarily surrendered' in March 1507.

wars.name: War of the League of Cambrai (papal front in Romagna)
wars.outcome: The League was formed in December 1508; Julius sent troops in May 1509 against Venetian forces in Romagna, and Agnadello (14 May 1509) led, per the page, to the papal recovery of territory.

wars.name: Julius II's war for Ferrara and the Holy League
wars.outcome: Julius's attempt to recover Ferrara ran from 1 September 1510 to 29 June 1512 (the page does not state the outcome; Ferrara was taken only in 1597); the Holy League was created on 4 October 1511; Louis XII won at Ravenna on 11 April 1512; in May 1512 the…

wars.name: Italian War of 1551-1559 (papal part)
wars.outcome: Philip II's armies defeated Paul IV's (Papal States page, paraphrased); no border moved.

wars.name: Sack of Rome (1527)
wars.outcome: Troops loyal to Charles V sacked Rome and imprisoned Clement VII; no border moved.

wars.name: French invasion of the Papal States (1796-1797)
wars.outcome: The Armistice of Bologna (1796) cost 21 million lire; the French seized the Legations; in February 1797 9,000 French soldiers invaded Papal Romagna and the pope accepted the Treaty of Tolentino of 19 February 1797, ceding Romagna, Ferrara and Bologna and…

wars.name: Neapolitan invasions of the Roman Republic
wars.outcome: The French occupied Rome on 11 February 1798 and proclaimed the republic on 15 February; Naples invaded in November 1798 (entering Rome unopposed on 29 November, beaten at Civita Castellana on 5 December and Otricoli on 9 December, French back in Rome on 14…

wars.name: Napoleonic annexation of the Papal States
wars.outcome: The Marche were annexed to the Kingdom of Italy on 2 April 1808; the rest, with Rome, to the First French Empire on 17 May 1809.

wars.name: Roman Republic and the French intervention of 1849
wars.outcome: Oudinot landed 8,000 to 10,000 French at Civitavecchia on 25 April 1849; the siege of Rome began in earnest on 1 June; the French entered Rome on 3 July 1849 and re-established the pope's temporal power; Garibaldi withdrew to San Marino on 2 July.

wars.name: Sardinian invasion of the Papal States (1860)
wars.outcome: Ultimatum 7 September, invasion 11 September, Castelfidardo 18 September, Ancona surrendered 29 September; plebiscites in the Marche and Umbria in November 1860 gave their annexation to Sardinia.

wars.name: Capture of Rome (1870)
wars.outcome: The French garrison was recalled in early August 1870; Italian troops crossed the frontier on 11 September, occupied Civitavecchia on 16 September, reached the walls on 19 September and breached them at Porta Pia on 20 September 1870; plebiscite 2 October and…

certainty.note: The Patrimony around Rome is firm; the exarchate, the Marche and Romagna were held through papal vicars and lords, and the Romagna page says papal control 'long remained only nominal'.

Pius IV established a specific identification for each province in 1559-1565 and a Congregation for Borders (1627) mediated jurisdictional disputes (Papal States page); the enclaves of Benevento, Pontecorvo, Avignon and the Comtat have…
French occupations, republics and annexations changed the lines almost yearly; no treaty line holds.
Restored by the Congress of Vienna; the frontier with the Kingdom of Sardinia and the Two Sicilies follows treaty lines until the 1859-60 and 1870 annexations.
